item.title: A new mining company wants to restart ore exports in Skagway
item.description: The proposal has revived concern over legacy contamination from ore shipping in the local port, and how to ensure it doesn't continue.

item.title: Juneau athletes head to Canada to compete in Arctic Winter Games
item.description: Four traditional snowshoers from Juneau will participate, alongside 270 other athletes from across Alaska.

item.title: Sen. Sullivan says he supports attack on Iran
item.description: He spoke of a limited role for the U.S. in regime change: "It's something that we can shape, but that's going to be ultimately up to the Iranian people."

item.title: Alaska House passes bill limiting AI sexual imagery and child social media use
item.description: The bill would ban AI-generated child sexual abuse material and, for adults, AI deepfakes and revenge porn. It also includes sharp limits on minors' use of social media.

item.title: Alaska House advances bill intended to boost workforce housing
item.description: House Bill 184 attempts to address Alaska's severe housing shortage by allowing AIDEA to invest in workforce housing with 5 or more units.

item.title: Alaska Folk Festival guest artist Willi Carlisle on what’s bringing him back to Juneau
item.description: Folk singer-songwriter Willi Carlisle is this year's guest artist at the 51st annual Alaska Folk Festival in April.

item.title: State lawmakers introduce bills to fight water pollution from cruise ships
item.description: The bills, from Sen. Jesse Kiehl and Rep. Sara Hannan, would push cruise lines to use cleaner fuel.

item.title: Juneau leaders ask Army Corps why it reversed on long-term glacial outburst flood solution
item.description: Agency staff say they want to look at an intermediate solution since the temporary levee could fail before a long-term solution is completed.

item.title: Community can weigh in on Juneau School District superintendent finalists this week
item.description: Members of the Juneau community have an opportunity to watch recorded interviews with finalists for Juneau schools superintendent and give feedback to the school board by Thursday.

item.title: Newscast – Monday, March 2, 2026
item.description: In this newscast: Members of the Juneau community have an opportunity to watch recorded interviews with finalists for Juneau schools superintendent and give feedback to the school board by Thursday; Since the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers pulled back its decision to design a lake tap that would put a stop to annual glacial outburst flooding in Juneau’s Mendenhall Valley, local and congressional leaders have pressed the agency to explain why; Crews are about half way done removing a colossal drill
